items.title: Margot Robbie & Kristoffer Borgli Team On ‘The Week Of Pain’ From A24 And Square Peg
items.summary:
Margot Robbie will star in The Week of Pain, a new film written and directed by Kristoffer Borgli for A24 and Ari Aster's Square Peg. Deadline reported the casting, noting that A24 will both finance and produce, with Square Peg's Lars Knudsen and Aster producing alongside Dilemma Films and Robbie's own LuckyChap.

Plot details remain undisclosed, which is standard practice for both Borgli and Square Peg. Borgli wrote the script himself, as he has on his previous features for the studio.

The project marks Borgli's third collaboration with A24, following 2023's Dream Scenario and The Drama, which the studio released in April. That film, starring Zendaya and Robert Pattinson, grossed $134 million worldwide and ranked among A24's biggest earners of the year.

Robbie has admired Borgli's work for some time and began talking with him about his next project well before the deal came together, according to Deadline. She has committed to shoot sometime in 2027, which places the film after her current slate.

That slate has been busy. Robbie's 2026 opened with Emerald Fennell's adaptation of Wuthering Heights, co-starring Jacob Elordi, which took in $240 million worldwide. She is now wrapping production on the Ocean's prequel opposite Bradley Cooper.

Robbie is represented by CAA, Entertainment 360 and Aran Michael Management, with attorney Jeff Bernstein; Borgli is repped by UTA. No release date has been set for The Week of Pain.

items.title: Watch Rosalía Perform a Lux Medley at the 2026 Latin Grammys
items.summary:
Rosalía opened the 2026 Latin Grammys with a medley drawn from Lux, her 2025 album. Wearing a golden gown and flanked by rows of dancers, the Catalan singer performed "La Rumba Del Perdón," "La Perla" and "Dios Es Un Stalker."

The performance set up a strong night for the record. Lux won five awards from seven nominations, including Album of the Year and Song of the Year for "La Perla."

The ceremony capped a busy stretch for Rosalía, as Pitchfork noted. Her role in Wet, a new film from director Alma Har'el, was confirmed this week, though shooting has not yet begun and few details about the project have surfaced.

On November 7, Rosalía marked the one-year anniversary of Lux by releasing a playlist of the music that fed into it, pulling from Kate Bush, Yung Lean, Mozart and Caetano Veloso, among others.

Video of the Latin Grammys performance is circulating online. Lux now stands as the most decorated album of the night.

items.title: IDK – “Welcome” (Feat. Eminem & Prod. J Dilla)
items.summary:
Maryland rapper IDK has released "Welcome," a track featuring Eminem built on an unreleased J Dilla beat. The song comes out through Eminem's Shady Records, and it marks the first time Eminem has rapped over a Dilla production — two decades after the producer's death.

The two came up in the same Detroit underground rap scene in the 1990s but never collaborated. As Stereogum pointed out, Dilla did work with Proof, Eminem's late mentor and D12 bandmate, and the pair briefly operated as a duo called the Funky Cowboys. Eminem handles only the hook on "Welcome," bending his tightly measured delivery to fit Dilla's characteristic drag.

IDK has spent the past year collecting co-signs from established figures. His concept album E.T.D.S. – Even The Devil Smiles featured Pusha T, Black Thought and the RZA, along with posthumous verses from MF DOOM and DMX. He later appeared beside Peter Gabriel on Everything Is Recorded's Beyond The Brilliant Haze.

In a statement about the song, IDK described talking to Dilla while making it. "When I first started working on this music, I remember looking up at my ceiling and saying thank you," he said. "I knew this was an important opportunity and a statement for hip-hop itself."

He also traced the release back to his own origins as a listener. "The first rap album I've ever owned was 50 Cent's Get Rich Or Die Tryin'. A Shady Records release," IDK said, adding that Eminem's verses were the first raps he set out to memorize.

IDK and Eminem shot a video for "Welcome" in Detroit with director Vuhlandes, and a short documentary clip showing the two in the studio accompanies the release.
